method: Read actual allergy introductory lessons 1-4 and cough triage, product-selection, supportive-care, congestion and interaction-safety teaching. Compare overlapping claims with product-specific source reviews already recorded in both journals. This is not whole-module verification.

findings.result: Both distinguish allergy pattern from viral illness and reject mucus color alone as evidence of bacterial infection. Cough adds explicit respiratory red flags and time-sensitive antiviral assessment.

Both specify distilled/sterile or boiled/cooled water, CDC one-minute/three-minutes-above-6500-feet durations, clean covered storage, device hygiene, gravity-device positioning and prompt assessment of neurologic/fever symptoms. FDA article longer boiling interval remains an explicitly documented source difference.

Cough standalone IR/ER schedules differ from exact prescription combination labeling. Allergy combinations preserve hydrochloride versus sulfate names and dose intervals. Retail base-weight purchase limits are explicitly separate from dosing. No cross-product substitution is endorsed.

findings.topic: Age labeling versus allergy guideline preference
findings.result: Both retain exact nasal product age permissions while distinguishing ARIA avoidance in children under12 for allergic rhinitis. Pediatric viral cold restrictions are not applied as blanket contraindications to separately labeled pediatric allergy products.

Cough explicitly attributes avoiding all pregnancy decongestants to UK SPS; allergy uses US society guidance to avoid pseudoephedrine in first trimester and seek individualized review later. These source-specific approaches are not represented as identical.

Cough specific Good Neighbor loratadine ODT example differs from allergy Claritin RediTabs/chewable and other ODT products; both require exact manufacturer/formulation review. Different excipient amounts are not an active-ingredient contradiction.

Both prohibit duplicate diphenhydramine including topical products and child-sedation use, and identify additive sedation/anticholinergic harm. Full first-generation book-topic closure still requires remaining precaution mapping.
